small_guidance:
- Add `@triton.autotune` over `(BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SPATIAL, num_warps, num_stages)` configs like `(32,64,4,2), (64,64,4,2), (32,128,8,2), (64,128,8,3), (128,32,4,2)`, keyed on `(OC, OUT_SPATIAL, IC*KD*KH*KW)`; the current `(32,64)` tile leaves the GEMM underutilized.
- Hoist the `ic` loop's weight base offset and prefetch `w_vals` once per `(kd,kh,kw)` outside the inner-most `ic` traversal by swapping loop order — make `ic` the K-reduction with a `BLOCK_IC` tile so `tl.dot` can be used (cast operands to fp16/bf16 only if accuracy allows; otherwise fp32 dot still beats scalar MACs).
- Fuse the spatial mean subtraction into the conv-transpose epilogue: accumulate a per-`(N,OC)` partial sum across spatial-tile programs via `tl.atomic_add` into a scratch buffer, then a tiny second kernel divides and subtracts — eliminates the extra full read/write pass currently done by `sub_mean_kernel`.
large_guidance:
- Reformulate as an im2col-style GEMM with `ic` as the K dimension and `tl.dot`: one program per `(N, OC tile, output-spatial tile)`, K-loop tiles `BLOCK_K = BLOCK_IC` (or `BLOCK_IC * tap_count`) so each iteration issues a real tensor-core/`tl.dot` MAC instead of the current scalar `w[:,None]*x[None,:]` outer products. This is where the 6.57 ms vs 1.78 ms baseline gap lives.
- Use a scatter-add formulation keyed on the input grid instead of the current gather: one program per `(N, IC tile, input-spatial tile)` computes `input × weight` outer products and scatters into the output via `tl.atomic_add`. This removes the per-output divmod/validity math (`id_r==0`, etc.) and naturally handles `stride>1` sparsity that currently wastes work in the gather.
- Make the kernel channels-last (NDHWC) end-to-end so both `x` loads along IC and `w` loads along OC are contiguous; fold BN scale/shift and the spatial-mean subtraction into one fused epilogue with a two-pass design (pass 1 writes out + accumulates per-(N,OC) sum via atomics; pass 2 subtracts mean). Keep `num_stages=2` and tiles ≤ `(64,64,32)` to stay under the 132 KB SMEM budget.
